source.title: Further Advantages of Data Augmentation on Convolutional Neural Networks

record.tranche_reason: Compares test accuracy with explicit regularization on versus off under different data augmentation, training-set sizes, and All-CNN depths; it tests a related regularization condition rather than dropout alone.
record.gate_note: The study reports qualitative outcomes from Figures 1 and 2 in the text, but does not give the plotted accuracy values. Cited results from prior work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: This follow-up uses the original V6 source's methodology: compare held-out accuracy with weight decay and dropout jointly enabled versus removed. It extends that comparison to reduced training sets and altered depths, directly testing V6's data-augmentation clause.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that augmentation transfers more readily across dataset-size and architecture changes, whereas retaining the original weight-decay and dropout settings can substantially reduce accuracy. Their explanation that retuning those regularizers would help is a hypothesis, not a tested result.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SGD with stated batch sizes and schedules, and compares weight decay plus dropout on versus off while varying data augmentation, data quantity, and architecture. It does not isolate dropout or test dropout alone.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported comparison changes with training-set size and architecture; the WRN result on 50% CIFAR-10 is a stated exception. Data augmentation level also varies in the experiments, though the text's comparison emphasizes heavier augmentation.
record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Neural Networks (ICANN) 2018
record.problems: The text does not provide numerical test accuracies for the results discussed; the quantitative results appear in figures. Weight decay and dropout are varied together, preventing attribution to dropout alone. It reports no uncertainty estimates.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Width beyond the zero-training-error threshold; changing depth does not test this.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects and adaptations of the training recipe.

Dropout's independent effect, suitably retuned dropout, dropout-rate sweeps and dropout-specific behavior on very small datasets. Joint removal cannot attribute the results to either regularizer separately.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removal of memorized examples versus random examples.

missing.what: WRN-28-10 trained on 50% of CIFAR-100 with heavier augmentation is omitted. Section 3.1 identifies only WRN on 50% CIFAR-10 as the exception to improved accuracy after joint removal, so the text supports the omitted condition as well.

record.verdict_notes: This study is distinct from the listed original V6 source, arXiv:1802.07042, although it shares authors and methodology. Numerical figure values and uncertainty cannot be recovered from the supplied text. The marginal R2 exception does not warrant a limits_scope verdict for a version that already allows accuracy to be preserved after joint removal.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy on natural versus random labels.
Width sweep past the interpolation threshold.

The study removes weight decay and dropout together, so it does not isolate dropout's effect. It does not test very small training sets as a dropout-specific regime, or compare different dropout amounts.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap.

rows.subject: All-CNN
rows.operation_detail: Compared training with weight decay and dropout to training without explicit regularization, using heavier data augmentation and reduced training sets.
rows.value: figure only; without explicit regularization generally outperformed the regularized counterpart, with differences greater at 10% training data
rows.note: The text summarizes the plotted results but does not state individual values for this architecture and condition.
rows.check: The qualitative direction is supported, but this aggregates two datasets and two training-set sizes. Split those conditions; exact accuracies are unavailable in the supplied text. The result concerns removing both regularizers, not dropout alone.

source_check.locator_found: Sections 2.1.1 and 3.1; Figure 1 caption and accompanying discussion.

rows.subject: WRN-28-10
rows.operation_detail: Compared training with weight decay and dropout to training without explicit regularization, using heavier data augmentation and reduced training sets.
rows.value: figure only; regularized model was marginally better (< 0.001)
rows.note: The authors characterize the difference as marginal; the exact plotted accuracies are not given in the text.
rows.check: The regularized model's advantage is explicitly marginal (<0.001 accuracy). This is consistent with nearly preserving accuracy after joint removal, as V6 allows; it does not establish a meaningful failure of that clause.

rows.subject: All-CNN
rows.size_stated: shallower: 374 K parameters; original: about 1.3 M parameters; deeper: 2.4 M parameters
rows.operation_detail: Compared test accuracy with weight decay and dropout to test accuracy without explicit regularization across shallower, original, and deeper All-CNN architectures.
rows.value: figure only; without explicit regularization, deeper architecture improved on the original and shallower architecture had a slight performance drop; with weight decay and dropout, the change of architecture caused a dramatic drop
rows.note: This compares the combined explicit-regularization setting against no explicit regularization; the text does not provide individual plotted values or isolate dropout.
rows.check: The text explicitly reports worse accuracy with both regularizers after depth changes. Split by dataset, depth and augmentation. Only augmented conditions directly test V6's augmentation clause. The comparison between depths alone cannot establish the effect of removing regularizers.

source_check.locator_found: Sections 2.1.1, 2.2 and 3.2; Figure 2 caption and accompanying discussion.
